answers.question: I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?
answers.answer:
Short answer: no to 40 mi and no to speedwork next week, but yes to building back soon.

Here is the shape I would like to follow:

| Week | Focus | Rough miles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| This week (Oct 26 – Nov 1) | All easy, light build | ~22 |
| Nov 2 – 8 | All easy, add one longer run | ~30 |
| Nov 9 – 15 | Easy plus strides, maybe one light tempo | ~35 |
| Nov 16 – 22 | First real 10K session, sharpen | ~38 |

A Thanksgiving 10K five weeks out is doable if you want it, but it would be a tune-up effort, not an all-out race; the deep soreness you had on race day takes time to clear even when the legs feel fresh walking around. Tell me this week whether the 10K is the target, whether you want a spring race to aim at, or whether you just want to run happy for a while, and I will build the next block around that.

new.analysis:
You did the recovery week right: three easy runs, zero pain, heart rate drifting back down to 133 on the easy runs from 139 before the race, and you came off Sunday feeling fresh. That is exactly the signal I wanted to see, and it is why we step up rather than repeat.

The reason we do not jump straight to 40 mi and reps is less about how you feel and more about what a marathon does under the surface. Muscle fibers, tendons and connective tissue keep rebuilding for three to four weeks after the race even when the legs feel bouncy, and the fastest way to sour that is a sudden load spike plus intensity. A 10 mi bump this week, then another 8, then another, keeps the rebuild honest.

On the Thanksgiving 10K, I am not against it, but I want to know what you want from the next few months before I shape sessions. A 10K five weeks out works best as a hard tune-up rather than a peak, and if you have a bigger goal after that (spring half, another marathon, a faster 5K) the block looks different. Answer in the check-in and I will map it out.

One small watch item: your easy pace drifted toward 9:50 on Sunday at only 139 bpm, which is right where you were pre-race. Fitness is still there. Let it stay there by keeping these next two weeks genuinely easy.
